summary: This work extends the Rothwarf-Taylor equations with a microwave power-dependent quasiparticle generation term to model the quality factor of superconducting resonators as a function of bath temperature and readout power. Measurements on NbN microstrip resonators with β-Ta terminations over a 40 dB power dynamic range and temperatures up to $T_c/2$ show excellent agreement with the model across the low-temperature saturation plateau, crossover, and high-temperature exponential decay regimes.
motivation: Superconducting resonators exhibit quality factors that deviate from Mattis-Bardeen predictions at low temperature, saturating rather than increasing; this is attributed to nonthermal quasiparticles generated by readout microwave power, which fundamentally limits device sensitivity.
method: The authors modified the Rothwarf-Taylor equations to include an explicit power-dependent phonon generation term $\Gamma_r = \eta P_{qp}/(V\Delta)$, deriving a quartic equation for the normalized quasiparticle density $u = n_{qp}/n^*$ that can be solved numerically for any $(T_b, P_r)$ combination to predict the internal quality factor $Q_i$.
result: Two NbN resonators (R1 and R2) with resonance frequencies of 3.7895 and 3.4290 GHz exhibited $Q_c \approx 19000$–21000 and $Q_r \approx 2500$–3400 at 100 mK, with quality factors spanning 40 dB in power and $T_b$ from 100 mK to $\sim 0.4$ K, all captured by the model using only a single temperature-independent loss parameter $Q_{other}$.
